method.unit: one run; stages are wall-clock differences between recorded timestamps, in seconds
method.start: fault_injected_at when recorded, else the timeline fault_injected phase, else the first failing Observer snapshot (from_first_failing_snapshot: a lower bound on detection, never imputed)
method.percentiles: median; p90 and p95 by nearest rank; null when n is 0
method.cold_call: a model call whose load_duration_seconds is over 1; calls without a recorded load duration are unclassified, never counted as warm

stages.planning: incident observed -> last planning-progress record (run folder only)
stages.model: sum of model call wall times; null when planning did not finish
stages.guard: planning end -> Guard ALLOW; includes the dependency check and the lab approval (pre-authorised before 4139385, automated auto-lab through the approval API from 4139385)
stages.decision: incident observed -> Guard ALLOW; in harness mode includes the scripted negative cases
stages.verification: Executor result -> end of the Verifier outcome window
stages.total: start -> end of the Verifier outcome window

limitations: One Windows/amd64 host with Docker Desktop and kind; runs share the host, cluster and model.
Mostly one fault type (invalid shipping PORT); from 870aa7d also the unscored catalog scenarios R2 and N1. Lab approval is pre-authorised or automated (auto-lab), so no human wait is included.
Runs before fault_injected_at was recorded start from the first failing snapshot, which understates detection.
Stages marked run_folder come from local run folders that are not committed and cannot be rechecked in CI.
Model time depends on the GPU, model and context size of the run; it is not portable to other hosts.

schema_notes: harness decision stage includes the scripted negative cases before the approved rollback
